title: How To Motivate Unmotivated Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin proposes a strategy for reaching chronically unmotivated students that departs from the usual advice of increased praise, encouragement, and pep talks. He argues true, sustaining motivation is intrinsic and comes from inspiration rather than external convincing, and that the standard advice—praise, reward, repeat—rarely works with hard-to-reach students. His method has two parts: first, stop excessive praise and pep-talks entirely; second, quietly watch for genuine evidence of quality work and respond with plain, honest, specific observations about the work itself ('That's a well-written sentence') rather than praise of the student. He stresses this feedback must be truthful and delivered matter-of-factly, without an exaggerated tone, since unmotivated students can detect phoniness. Over time, this approach is said to spark intrinsic pride in the work itself, gradually drawing reluctant students into genuine engagement.
points: Standard motivational advice—praise, encouragement, reward, repeat—is described as largely ineffective with chronically unmotivated students.
True, lasting motivation is framed as intrinsic inspiration rather than something achieved by external convincing or cheerleading.
Step one of the strategy: stop excessive praise, pep-talks, and 'talking students through' their capabilities.
Step two: quietly watch for genuine evidence of quality work and respond with plain, honest, specific observations about the work itself, delivered without an exaggerated tone.
The approach is intended as a long-term process, not a one-time fix, gradually building intrinsic pride and engagement rather than immediate compliance.
quotes: Trying and failing to motivate unmotivated students is a common frustration among teachers.
True motivation, however—that which is internal and sustaining—doesn’t develop through convincing. It isn’t about ramped-up enthusiasm or flattery.
The first step is to stop the flow of excessive and over-the-top praise.
You’re going to give plain and honest feedback about the evidence you see on the page or screen.
Now, it’s important to note that it must be true. The least motivated in particular can recognize phoniness from a mile a way.
By truthfully pointing out quality when you see it, you spark their once dormant intrinsic motivational engine to life. You wake up the sleeping giant.
